package_info.why_malicious: These package versions were compromised via stolen npm account tokens, allowing attackers to inject malicious code that automatically downloads and runs a cryptominer (XMRig) on installation, exfiltrates system/network information, and attempts to evade detection by blending into the filesystem and limiting CPU usage.

execution_context.file_location: support.js (@rspack/core), config.js (@rspack/cli), unknown file in vant

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads the XMRig cryptominer binary from a remote GitHub repository and writes it to disk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Package installation should not download and execute external binaries, especially cryptominers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal postinstall scripts are used for setup, not for fetching and running third-party executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may download platform-specific binaries for legitimate CLI tools, but never for cryptominers.
key_indicators: Downloads binary from external source during install

execution_context.file_location: support.js (@rspack/core), config.js (@rspack/cli), unknown file in vant

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Performs a network request to ipinfo.io to retrieve the victim's IP address, geolocation, and network details.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reconnaissance of the victim's environment is not expected during package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect or exfiltrate geolocation/network information on install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or telemetry libraries may collect environment info, but not at install time and not without disclosure.

execution_context.file_location: support.js (@rspack/core), config.js (@rspack/cli), unknown file in vant

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Renames the downloaded XMRig binary to a less suspicious name to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscating the presence of a cryptominer by renaming it is a clear anti-forensics technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries are not renamed to generic or misleading names post-download.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate software may rename files for compatibility, but not to hide malicious intent.

execution_context.file_location: support.js (@rspack/core), config.js (@rspack/cli), unknown file in vant

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes the cryptominer with parameters to limit CPU usage to 75% of available threads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running a cryptominer on user systems is inherently malicious; limiting CPU usage is an evasion tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should mine cryptocurrency on user hardware.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall scripts that download and execute external binaries
Network requests to cryptocurrency miner repositories (e.g., GitHub xmrig releases)
Access to geolocation APIs (e.g., ipinfo.io) during install
Renaming of downloaded binaries to generic or misleading names
Execution of binaries with CPU usage limiting parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that download and execute external binaries, especially from known cryptominer sources. Flag any network requests to cryptocurrency mining repositories or geolocation APIs during install. Watch for the creation or renaming of suspicious files (e.g., /tmp/vant_helper, /tmp/xmrig) and the execution of binaries with CPU-limiting parameters. Use static and dynamic analysis to inspect package scripts for these behaviors.
